problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over an operational window of 18 weeks.  
The starting stockpile at the commencement of the planning interval is 81 kiloliters.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 18 \), the supplier permits the company to submit a procurement request whose volume must be between 6 and 25 kiloliters.  
Nevertheless, every request issued will undergo a lead time of 3 weeks before it becomes available to meet consumption or replenish the stockpile.  
The consumption of the additive in each week is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: consumption 16 kiloliters  
* Week 2: consumption 16 kiloliters  
* Week 3: consumption 49 kiloliters  
* Week 4: consumption 53 kiloliters  
* Week 5: consumption 17 kiloliters  
* Week 6: consumption 29 kiloliters  
* Week 7: consumption 52 kiloliters  
* Week 8: consumption 29 kiloliters  
* Week 9: consumption 47 kiloliters  
* Week 10: consumption 33 kiloliters  
* Week 11: consumption 21 kiloliters  
* Week 12: consumption 59 kiloliters  
* Week 13: consumption 10 kiloliters  
* Week 14: consumption 52 kiloliters  
* Week 15: consumption 58 kiloliters  
* Week 16: consumption 40 kiloliters  
* Week 17: consumption 35 kiloliters  
* Week 18: consumption 35 kiloliters  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied consumption will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning horizon, additive quantities may be fractional, and the total volume of physically held stock at any moment must not surpass the depot capacity of 81 kiloliters.  

In week 13, the maximum procurement volume is restricted to 10 kiloliters.  
In week 14, the physically available stockpile must be no less than 26 kiloliters.  

The aggregate expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement cost, which is 3 per kiloliter ordered; the storage cost, which is 2 per kiloliter of stock transferred from one week to the next; and the shortage penalty, which is 12 per kiloliter of unmet consumption. Determine the optimal procurement volume for each week and monitor the ensuing stockpile and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
